prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of a quiet poetry zine page lying on a soft linen surface under a warm window light. The paper is soft ivory, slightly thicker than photocopier stock, with deckled edges on two sides.

Subject:
A poetic cut-up arrangement on the page: narrow strips of photocopied typewriter text, each with a different age-yellowing, arranged in a loose waterfall pattern down the center. A small pencil illustration of a bird in flight sits in the top-right corner. Three pressed petals are taped at the lower margin. Ink-brush marks in pale grey connect some strips like threads.

Important details:
Each typewriter strip must look cut from different source papers — some darker, some more yellowed, some with a curved tear. Pale grey ink-brush threads must bleed into paper fibers. Pencil bird must be restrained, unfinished. Pressed petals carry believable color pigment loss.

Use case:
Independent single image in the Collage Moods package, representing the poetic cut-up voice.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names, no vector lines, no crisp digital alignment, no symmetry, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
title: Poetry Cut-up Page
description: A quiet zine page of cut-up typewriter strips arranged like a waterfall, with pencil bird and pressed petals.
